neighbours.label: Best guess: ' guess' or the end of a clause when two people take turns ('You and I take turns, and then you guess'); ' guess' with no turn-taking stays quiet.
fire: You and your sister take turns, and then you guess the word.
Sit with a partner and take turns, then you guess the song.
My brother and I took turns, and then I guessed the name.
You and a friend take turns, and then you guess the winner.
The two of you alternate, and then you guess the number.
We swap roles each round, and then you guess the card.
Each of you goes in turn, and then you guess the color.
You two trade places, and then you guess the face.
quiet: You and your sister sit down, and later you guess the word.
Sit with a book and relax, then you find the song.
My brother and I went home, and then I guessed the name.
You and a friend go shopping, and then you buy the shirt.
The two of you leave early, and then you phone the office.
We stay late each night, and then you lock the door.
Each of you has a map, and then you follow the road.
You two wash up, and then you set the table.

notes: A sparse pole with no consistent token on the card: ' what', ' of', ' letting', ' on', ' other', ' which'. Apart from one ' on' (' capitalized on' read 0.44 once, then 0.01, so I dropped it), only two turn-taking sentences read above 0.3 in probes (0.31, 0.35), and 'switch places' read 0.08. The output direction promotes ' two', ' mutual', ' mutually' and suppresses ' everyone', ' people', ' others', which fits a two-party reading but is weak support. Expected to fail.
